The '''49th Academy Awards''' were presented Monday, March 28, 1977, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], hosted by [[Richard Pryor]], [[Ellen Burstyn]], [[Jane Fonda]], and [[Warren Beatty]]. Both ''[[Network (1976 film)|Network]]'' and ''[[All the President's Men (film)|All the President's Men]]'' won four Oscars, the most of the evening, but lost [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], as well as [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Editing]], to ''[[Rocky]]''.

''Network'' became the second film (after ''[[A Streetcar Named Desire (1951 film)|A Streetcar Named Desire]]'') to win three acting Oscars, the last to do so until ''[[Everything Everywhere All at Once]]'', and the last, as of the [[97th Academy Awards]], to receive five acting nominations. It was also the eleventh of fifteen films (to date) to receive [[List of films with all four Academy Award acting nominations|nominations in all four acting categories]]. [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] winner [[Peter Finch]] became the first posthumous acting winner, having suffered a fatal heart attack in mid-January. With only five minutes and two seconds of screentime, [[Beatrice Straight]] set a record for the shortest performance ever to win an acting Oscar ([[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]]). [[Paddy Chayefsky]] won his third solo writing Oscar for ''Network'', a record that remains to this day.

[[Sylvester Stallone]] became the first person since [[Orson Welles]] to receive nominations for writing and acting for the same film (''Rocky''), losing in both categories to ''Network''.

[[Piper Laurie]] was nominated for Best Supporting Actress for ''[[Carrie (1976 film)|Carrie]]'' (1976), her first role since her Best Actress-nominated performance in ''[[The Hustler]]'' (1961), thus being nominated for two consecutive roles, fifteen years apart.

[[Lina Wertmüller]] became the first woman nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for ''[[Seven Beauties]]'', which was also nominated for [[Academy Award for Best International Feature Film|Best Foreign Language Film]]. With her win for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] as the composer for the love theme "[[Evergreen (Love Theme from A Star Is Born)|Evergreen]]" from ''[[A Star Is Born (1976 film)|A Star Is Born]]'', [[Barbra Streisand]] became the first woman to be honored in the category, and, as of the [[97th Academy Awards]], the only person to have won Academy Awards for both acting and songwriting (following her [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] win for ''[[Funny Girl (film)|Funny Girl]]'' at the [[40th Academy Awards]]).

No honorary awards were given this year.

[[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] held the rights to the Oscars from [[33rd Academy Awards|1961]] to [[42nd Academy Awards|1970]] and regained them for the [[48th Academy Awards|1976 event]]. For the second straight year, the ceremony was scheduled directly opposite the [[1977 NCAA Division I Basketball Championship Game|NCAA championship basketball game]] on [[NBC Sports|NBC]], won by [[1976–77 Marquette Warriors men's basketball team|Marquette]] in [[Al McGuire]]'s final game as head coach.
